title: Dementia friendly apothecaries as a resource for mental health in the elderly
summary:
Background and Aim: Dementia is a major challenge for both individuals and the healthcare system. The DARE study examines whether digital dementia screening in community pharmacies can help detect the condition early and improve participants’ quality of life.
Methods: About 1,020 pharmacy customers with memory concerns across 14 pharmacies in the Munich area will be included. On-site digital screening assesses dementia and related risk factors. The study evaluates how screening affects quality of life, healthcare use, diagnoses, and medication at 12 and 24 months. In addition, participants and pharmacy staff are interviewed to explore the acceptance and feasibility of the screening.

interventions.name:
Pharmacy customers and patients aged 60 or older reporting cognitive complaints in urban and rural community pharmacies in the Munich area, Germany, will be included. On-site digital screening for dementia and related risk factors is conducted at all participating pharmacies.
Participants complete

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Pharmacy customers or patients of age ≥60 years and of any sex or ethnicity
- Presence of subjective cognitive decline
= Operationalized as a positive response to at least one of the three initial questions of the Subjective Cognitive Decline Questionnaire (SCD-Q17)
- Ability to understand study procedures and to provide written informed consent, as judged appropriate by the pharmacists/pharmaceutical staff.
Exclusion criteria:
- Prior diagnosis of dementia (with or without supporting pathological evidence) as documented in medical records or confirmed by a physician
- Insufficient proficiency in the German language
- Significant visual impairments
- Significant fine motor skill disorders.
